scenario.prompt_to_agent:
pc2 (200.1.1.2) lost all connectivity to the partner network, and
the partner reports pc1 (195.11.14.2) cannot reach pc2 either.
Our NOC tried to inspect router2 but vtysh commands on it error
out entirely -- they cannot even display the routing table. pc2
can still ping router2's address 200.1.1.1. Find what broke.

injection.action: kill the entire FRR stack (watchdog, zebra and bgpd) on router2
injection.command: pkill -9 watchfrr; pkill -9 zebra; pkill -9 bgpd

scenario.ground_truth:
Affected component: router2 FRR routing stack (zebra + bgpd,
  watchfrr included)
Mechanism: the whole FRR service on router2 is dead -- not just
  one daemon. With bgpd gone the eBGP session's TCP connection
  closes, so router1 immediately drops the session and withdraws
  200.1.1.0/24; pc1's traffic toward pc2 then dies at router1 with
  no route, and pc2's replies/pings toward 195.11.14.0/24 have no
  usable end-to-end path either. With zebra ALSO dead, vtysh has
  no daemon left to attach to, so it fails outright -- unlike a
  bgpd-only crash, where vtysh stays responsive via zebra. (A
  stale kernel route to 195.11.14.0/24 may linger on router2,
  since zebra died without cleaning up; end-to-end traffic still
  fails because router1 has withdrawn 200.1.1.0/24.) router2's
  kernel itself is alive: it still answers on its connected
  addresses, e.g. pc2 -> 200.1.1.1.
Localization: router2
Root cause: FRR routing stack (zebra and bgpd) not running on
  router2
Fix: restart FRR on router2 (`service frr restart`)
scenario.fix_spec:
Restart the FRR service on router2 (`service frr restart`). This brings back
watchfrr, zebra and bgpd from /etc/frr/frr.conf; the eBGP session to router1
re-establishes, the inter-AS prefixes are re-exchanged, and pc1 reaches pc2
normally. router1 needs no change.

agent.diagnosis_text:
**Affected component:** The entire FRR routing daemon suite (`watchfrr`, `zebra`, `bgpd`) on router2 is down — all three processes are absent from the process table.

**Mechanism:** With `bgpd` dead on router2, it cannot establish or maintain the BGP session with router1. Router1's BGP neighbor for router2 is stuck in the `Active` state (continuously retrying), meaning router1 never learns the `200.1.1.0/24` prefix. Without that BGP-learned route, router1 has no forwarding path to pc2's subnet and returns "Destination Net Unreachable" to pc1 for every packet destined for `200.1.1.2`. Simultaneously, with `zebra` down on router2, its kernel routing table has no BGP-installed route to `195.11.14.0/24`, so packets from pc2 toward pc1 have no next-hop and are silently dropped — explaining the timeout. The reported `vtysh` failure is a direct consequence: `vtysh` connects to the FRR UNIX sockets, and with no daemon alive, every vtysh command immediately errors out.

**Localization:** router2, FRR daemon suite (`/etc/init.d/frr` or `systemctl frr`). Router1 and both hosts are healthy; pc2 can still reach router2's interface IP `200.1.1.1` because kernel L3 forwarding for directly-attached subnets does not require FRR.

**Root cause:** All FRR processes on router2 have crashed or been killed, taking down the BGP control plane and eliminating inter-AS route exchange entirely.

**Fix:** Restart FRR on router2 with `systemctl restart frr` (or `/etc/init.d/frr restart`). Once `zebra` and `bgpd` come up, the BGP session with router1 will re-establish, both routers will exchange their network prefixes, and full pc1 ↔ pc2 connectivity will be restored.
